newsitem.title: INDIA: India's L&T raises $115 mln loan-ANZ.
newsitem.headline: India's L&T raises $115 mln loan-ANZ.

text.p: Indian engineering and construction giant Larsen & Toubro Ltd (L&T) raised $115 million through a syndicated term loan, ANZ Grindlays Bank said on Friday.
The loan was arranged by ANZ Investment Bank, the Bank of Nova Scotia Asia Ltd, State Bank of India and Sumitomo Bank, ANZ Grindlays Bank said in statement.
"The facility has a door-to-door life of eight years and an average life of seven years," it said.
"It has a step-up interest structure, with the interest margins on the loan increasing from 60 bppa (basis points per annum) to 123.5 bppa over the tenor facility," it said.
The funds are to be utilised for financing construction of the company's power plants at the Awarpur and Gujarat cement works and for import of capital goods, the statement said.
The loan was initially launched for $75 million and was substantially oversubscribed. In view of the positive response from the market, the size was raised to $115 million, it said.
Fourteen participants from eight countries in North America, Europe, Middle East, South East Asia and Japan contributed to the loan, ANZ Grindlays said.
"The success of this transaction is proof of L&T's excellent standing among international debt providers," it quoted Y.M. Deosthale, director of L&T, as saying.
"The loan has unique staggered pricing structure and the overall pricing is extremely fine," he said.

"India is a very important market for the ANZ group and our commitment is demonstrated as the number one arranger in the league tables for Indian debt transactions," the statement quoted Rana Kapoor, general manager and head of corporate finance at ANZ Grindlays in India, as saying.
ANZ has raised over $4.3 billion debt for Indian corporates since 1990, the bank said.
